evals.prompt: Before I merge feature/iptw-weights into main, I want an adversarial pass on the diff. It changes R/weights.R (stabilized IPTW with truncation at the 1st/99th percentile) and R/outcome_model.R (svyglm with robust SEs). This feeds the primary estimand in our sepsis readmission paper, so I care about ways it silently produces wrong effect estimates. target:code depth:quick
evals.expected_output: A read-only adversarial synthesis of the branch diff against its merge base, with local and peer coverage labeled, concrete failure scenarios for the weighting/outcome code, and no edits made.
expectations: Does not edit, stage, or commit any file in the repository

Final report uses the exact section structure: Adversarial review header with Target, Mode, Coverage, Research grounding, then Confirmed findings, Converged after rebuttal, Not debated due to budget, Harness disagreement, Residual risks and verification gaps
Every reported finding names a specific file:line location, a trigger, a consequence, and a confidence of 50, 75, or 100

Coverage line states either the peer harness used or an explicit local-only reason (e.g. local-only (peer unavailable) with the failed availability check); it never claims a peer review that did not run
With depth:quick, performs no rebuttal rounds

evals.prompt: can you get codex to independently tear apart docs/plans/2026-09-30-001-feat-target-trial-emulation-plan.md? its the plan for our TTE of early vs delayed dialysis in AKI using the CLIF extract. i want the load-bearing assumptions challenged (grace period, clone-censor-weight choice, the eligibility window). peer:codex
evals.expected_output: A plan-target adversarial review that runs Codex read-only as the named peer (or stops and asks if Codex is unavailable), challenging premises, load-bearing decisions, and omitted alternatives in the plan.
expectations: Treats the supplied .md path as target:plan and reviews only that document

Runs the Codex availability check (codex login status) before dispatch; if it fails, stops, reports the failed check, and asks whether to retry later or continue local-only rather than silently falling back
Captures peer output under /tmp/methodsmith/method-adversarial-review/<run-id>/ and validates it with scripts/validate_peer_artifact.py before using it in synthesis
Findings focus on plan-level challenges (premises, load-bearing decisions, reversal cost, omitted alternatives) rather than code style
Does not pass raw patient-level CLIF data or credentials into the peer prompt

evals.prompt: Run an adversarial review. There are two candidate docs I was working on: docs/plans/sap-v2.md and docs/brainstorms/2026-09-12-frailty-index-requirements.md, plus some uncommitted changes in analysis/frailty.py. Just pick whatever makes sense and also fix anything critical you find.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses to guess among multiple candidate targets, asks the user to specify target:code or target:plan <path>, and declines to apply fixes because the workflow is read-only.
expectations: Asks the user to choose target:code or target:plan <path> instead of choosing among the multiple candidate documents itself
Does not edit analysis/frailty.py or any plan document, stating the review is read-only
Mentions that actionable code findings can be routed to method-review and plan findings to method-doc-review or method-plan if follow-through is wanted
Does not dispatch a peer harness before the target is resolved
